item.title: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Readers & Reviewers: Re: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Readers & Reviewers
item.content:encoded:
Heya Four!

Welcome to the site! There's a lot of talented artists who make SCP content - if you like animations, there's a few YouTubers who create them such as Lord Bung, but also some animators here on the site you can find by going through the various art pages! Regardless though, joining the site so you can rate and review skips is a great reason to join, and you're right that there's absolutely no rush to write anything just yet. A great place to start is right where you said - reading - in order to learn what skips do well, what aspects you like, and what you'd like to accomplish in your own skips. I've left you with a reading list to help take you through the recent articles, I hope you find it helpful! All in all, thanks for sharing with us, and enjoy your time here on the site.

+Here are some places to start.
-Hope this helps!

Maybe you've already seen these before, maybe you haven't, but hopefully something here is of use to you. Of course, if you have any questions, feel free to reach out!

The newest, freshest material can be found on the Most Recently Created page. If that updates a little too frequently for you though and you want more of a look at what remains popular, you can also try the Top Rated New Pages.

If you want to see what other folks in the community like, there's the User-Curated Lists. Here you can find things the community has put together and deemed a good read. Or maybe you want to give some underrated articles some love? Try out the Underread and Underrated page.

Enjoy large hubs and working your way through them? Some cool hubs include the Guide Hub for things that cover the Site itself, Site News Hub for updates on all sorts of monthly Site content, Canon Hub for all the various canons, GoI Format Hub for all your GoI needs, and Tales Hub for your favorite tales.

Finally, if you find an author you love from any of this and want to see more from them, you can find them in the Authors' Pages section. If they're not on that list, try the statistic site, scpper.com.

item.title: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Readers & Reviewers: Re: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Readers & Reviewers
item.content:encoded:
Hello Hinroe!

Welcome to the site! There's a lot of great content creators over on YouTube, I'm glad one of them could inspire you to come join the site itself! And I would personally love to see some more tale writers as well, I think there's a lot of unexplored content that can be covered in tales that skips have a harder time approaching! Focusing on the personal aspects of the MTF units sounds like a great place to start, I wish you the best and have left you some writer's resources to help you get started. Keep in mind to work at whatever pace works best for you, and that there's no rush to contribute. All that being said though, I hope you enjoy your time here on the site!

+A gift of resources just for you
-Hope this helps!

Maybe you've already seen these before, maybe you haven't, but hopefully something here is of use to you. Of course, if you have any questions, feel free to reach out!

First off, there are some required readings for all site authors. Consider giving them a read, as well as all the other helpful guides on this Guide Hub. The more familiar you are with the processes that take place on the Site, the better your chances of success are!

Now that that's done - Got an idea? Or maybe a few? You can create a Sandbox page to store all your ideas and drafts in an orderly fashion.

Okay, but maybe you're not sure if your concept is ready to be fleshed out, or perhaps it just needs some heavy refinement. If that's the case, you can run things by the community in the Ideas and Brainstorming forum.

Once you believe you have a solid draft, you can go ahead and make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Keep in mind though you should check the stickied posts first on how best to use each of the forums.

Best of luck writing!

Hey! I joined this wiki because I've always been fascinated by the idea of the Foundation and SCPs. item.title: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers: Re: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello y'all, my name is DrTweed. I originally found this site when I was 13 and I completely forgot about it until I saw references to the SCP Foundation on TikTok believe it or not.

I don't read a lot anymore or write so much either, but I'd like to see myself as an above average writer. My biggest influence for writing style has most definitely been H.P. Lovecraft. I'm also a biochemistry major trying to become a drug researcher/developer so I thought it'd be fun to read and write some "science-y SCPs."

I really just hope I can bring a part of me to the site and leave a mark somehow!

As for the elements, Earth definitely represents me the best just because I'm a stubborn and enduring person and I feel like Earth/rocks personify that.

item.title: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers: Re: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello! I'm Arlin Bradley. I'm a historian who adores academic prose. My experience writing pulp horror makes SCP an interesting intersection of interests for me. On one hand, I wanna write horrific new SCPs and Tales until my fingers start bleeding. However, I'm also interested in editing existing stories (spelling, grammar, etc.) to improve the overall quality of the site.

Random facts for the nosey! My favorite horror movie is Tucker and Dale vs. Evil, my favorite horror manga is Tomie by Junji Ito, and my favorite horror novel is Frankenstein by Mary Shelley. My top-rated creepypasta, Plaguespreader, peaked at #11 on r/shortscarystories and currently sits at #18. Your Name by Makoto Shinkai has thrice made me cry and I'll defend romantic comedies to my dying breath.

item.title: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers: Re: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello! While my account name is ShadyFoliose, I definitely use "Shady" in all of my online names so I usually respond with that.

I've been a fan of the SCP community and following its development since around 2010 so I'm really excited to now be apart it! I finally made up my mind that I would like to contribute to this project, ideally through writing but really in whatever way I can.

I'm a geology major, biology minor (botany focused), and GIS minor. Despite my STEM focus, I have been writing as a hobby for quite a while with more horror themes. I look forward to hopefully writing some tales.

Finally, if I was a classical element I'd have to say water. I've been a competitive swimmer and swim coach so most of my life has been water oriented. I also consider myself rather "flexible" with most things.

I look forward to writing and working with/engaging with everyone!

item.title: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers: Re: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hey Agent Moon5, welcome officially to the site! Everyone gets around to doing things at their own pace, so no need to be concerned there. I'm sure you can utilize one or all of those interests in an SCP you write to make it even more interesting, best of luck!
As for writing, just make sure you go through the proper greenlighting process on the idea forums first. Remember that there is no rush, and you should take time familiarizing yourself with how Series 6 articles are formatted. We are a rather unique bunch so I'm sure just reading and being a part of the community will be rather fun for you! For my recommendation, you should check out [[|SCP-5100]its about some strange phenomenon that is happening in China.

+ Resources
- Hide Resources

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts.

Sandbox

For hashing out concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by the community if you need help refining your concept.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success!

As far as reading is concerened, you might want to check out our Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular, recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community.

Best of luck!

item.title: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers: Admin Post - Info - Open
item.content:encoded:
Hello, my name is Dr. Ash Greywhind, I would like to be called Dr. Grey.

Obligatory note that the SCP wiki is not a roleplaying site—users in the forums don't refer to site members with in-universe names, and won't append titles like "doctor" that don't appear in usernames.

If you would like to be addressed with a certain name/title, make that your username (provided it follows the Join the Site rules).
